name: ANTITHROMBIN -III ANTIGEN
interpretation:
1. Anti-thrombin is a glycoprotein of a molecular weight of approximately 58,000 daltons, synthesized in the liver. As an inhibitor of thrombin, the
activity of Anti-thrombin is dramatically enhanced by heparin. It also inhibits factor Xa and to a lesser extent the factors IXa, XIa, XIIa as well as
plasmin and kallikrein.
2. Anti-thrombin has been considered an important parameter in thromboembolic disorder.
3. At present, the Anti-thrombin congenital deficiencies are classified into four categories as below:-

Type of Deficiency   Protein Amount Biological Activity  Remarks
I Decreased Decreased More frequent case
II RS (reactive site)  Normal  Decreased Anomaly of the reactive site

II PE (pleiotropic effect) Decreased Decreased Dysfunctional protein and at reduced quality

4. Anti-thrombin III deficiency can be also due to:-
• Decreased synthesis - as occurs with acute and chronic liver disease.
• Increased catabolism - as in disseminated intravascular coagulation and nephrotic syndrome.
• Administration of drugs like oral contraceptives, chemotherapeutics, anti-coagulants and L- asparaginase treatments.
• Physiological reduction in late pregnancy.
• Congenital deficiency and production of structurally abnormal Anti-thrombin III is also known.

5. Individuals with 40-50% of the normal levels of Anti-thrombin III are considered to be deficient and are susceptible to  thrombosis.
6. Anti-thrombin III is an acute phase reactant.
7. The Anti-thrombin level in women up to the menopausal period is a little lower than that in men.A diminution of this level  is observed during pregnancy.
8 .In men, the Anti-thrombin level decreases with age.
9. In children the Anti-thrombin level is normally low until the age of 6 months; at this time it reaches the adult level
